title: Bix at the piano and notating his compositions
summary: Challis notated Bix's five piano pieces exactly and describes them as pianistic yet orchestral with a cornet-like melody.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But Eastwood Lane, I become more familiar with it, but I was made acquainted with it through Beiderbecke, I would say. He used to -- if we would go to a new job, if we got to a job and there was a piano there, or if after the job, there was a piano there and it's nice, he used to liked to sit down and play it. And he would do this, and he could play -- he was a fine pianist, but not any particular style. He was no Arthur Shutt or no Frankie Signorelli, anything like that.

All those good piano players, but yet he had his own, and sometimes, just a few little notes voiced. Voicing to him was very important and his chords were constructed correctly. I notated all his things and there aren't many, only five and I put them down exactly the way he played them. I made a point of that. They are unorthodox in some places.
His runs, but now he had the ear and the idea of the sound for all this. It was all orchestral and I think

Eastwood Lane is the same way. You can tell the way they put things in the left hand and fill out here, and it was not -- it was not instrumental in the sense that you find -- they didn't know anything about the fiddle, so they don't know any-things about the bowings, the fingerings and so forth of the fiddle, nor of the clarinet. It's put down harmonically.
It's pianistic, and it's pianistic trying to be orchestral, if I'm making any kind of sense.
Yes. Well, what kind of effect do you think his cornet experience had on all this. It was a separate thing?

Now, when Bix wrote his piano things, he had one line melody, that was very few pianistic things in there, but that melody stuck out, and I would say that you could pick out some of these things, and there would be like he could play it on the cornet.
